facts.text: `tern-plugins/code-puppy/python-plugin/register_callbacks.py` registers `_on_startup` for the `startup` phase and `_on_render_final_response` for the `render_final_response` phase.
`_candidate` gates the TSP probe on `TERM_PROGRAM=tern`, no `TMUX`/`STY`/`ZELLIJ`, and `TERN_TSP` not `0`; `_probe` also requires stdin and stdout to be TTYs and restores the tty in a `finally`.
`parse_hello_reply` accepts a v1 `hello` reply only if it arrives before the DA1 reply and advertises the `flow` feature and the `md` kind.
`build_flow_messages` emits open (`listen: False`), one `md` frame, and close-keep APC messages, and returns None when the frame exceeds `_MAX_FRAME_BYTES` (60000), so Rich is used instead.

`_on_render_final_response` claims output only for the `agent_response` banner with non-empty content and returns `{"handled": True}` after writing; other cases return None so core Rich rendering runs.
The Python plugin draws only final non-streamed agent responses. Streamed text, tool output, diffs, thinking and sub-agent output stay Rich, and approvals are not touched.
The Python plugin is not installed automatically. It is loaded from `~/.code_puppy/plugins/tern`, set up by manually symlinking or copying `tern-plugins/code-puppy/python-plugin` there.

The core hook `on_render_final_response` in `code_puppy/callbacks.py` is called from `display_non_streamed_result` and `RichConsoleRenderer._render_agent_response`; a plugin claims output by returning `{"handled": True}`.

Direct Tern wiring in Code Puppy core (the `cli_runner.py` probe call and `code_puppy/tern_surface.py`) is no longer part of the working integration; core carries only the generic `render_final_response` hook.
The pre-hook direct-TSP edits are preserved outside both repos at `/Users/swarm/Work/Clover/_tern_legacy_backup_20261011_153130` and should not be removed while that is the only saved copy.
